title: Majestic Defense
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the six-piece position after g4+ and the accepted rook sacrifice. Checked the unique winning Kf4 king escort, actual e2 pawn mate, and two drawing deviations. Earlier rook maneuver remains source context.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius will be able [music] to find the incredible win that black has in this position. Black is only left with two pawns against a pawn, a rook, and a knight. But, he can play pawn to f2 and now be only one step away from getting a new queen. White has to use the rook, but surprisingly enough, it is really hard for the rook to stop the pawn. For example, rook to c1 would fail to the precise e3 because two connected passed pawns that have surpassed either the third or sixth rank are going to be unstoppable even for a rook. And so, black will be able to promote and win this game. So, after that pawn push, white has nothing better but to start checking the black king and hope that he can keep checking the king forever. But, actually the king can find shelter behind his own pawn. And now, there are going to be no more safe checks for the white rook. So, is this it? Is black simply out of [music] the woods in this position? Well, not yet because white has the brilliant rook to [laughter] f5 stepping right behind the pawn that is trying to promote but sacrificing the rook to the black king. First of all, if black now tries to promote by pushing e3, white will be able to play g3, king to g2, >> [music] >> and this time although black promotes, white can at least win the other pawn. And with best play, this rook and pawn and king will be able to hold back the black queen. Okay, so what? Black can simply accept the sacrifice and take the f5 rook. What's the bright idea? Well, the idea is to play g4 check, force black to move the king, and then play king to g2 stopping the black pawn. And believe it or not, this would be a draw. Black can never push without allowing white to win the pawns. And so, this will give the white knight enough time to sacrifice itself for one of the pawns and enter this drawn king and pawn endgame. But black has not used all of his cards quite yet. And after G4 check, he can play the extremely precise king F4, leaving the pawn where it is because now after king to G2, he can play king E3 defending the pawn with the king and threatening king to E2, which would prepare the promotion to a new queen and black would win. So after king to E3, >> [music] >> white is forced to play king to F1 physically stopping it from promoting. Now black can pave the way for the other pawn and also block the white king in its place, which means that no matter what white does, in a matter of two moves, this is going to be a beautiful king and pawn checkmate.
